output.brief: The wrong dates were not an operator or printer problem. Printer records show that from 4 Oct (22:10) every Veltranol job received a 36-month shelf life from PackBridge, before any operator touched it. Nobody overrode anything, including two permanent-staff jobs on Line 1. Jobs by agency operators after the firmware change, up to 3 Oct, were correct. The ERP shows Regulatory Affairs entered 36 months on 3 Oct, valid only from 1 Mar 2027, while the current value stays 24. The most likely cause is that the future-dated value reached the line early, despite the vendor's claim that this can't happen. I'm fairly sure, but the exact mechanism inside PackBridge is unconfirmed. The director's plan to remove and warn agency staff would punish the wrong people and leave the fault in place. Do now: lock the Veltranol shelf-life record to 24, hold all Veltranol lots packed since 4 Oct, including the two Line 1 lots in the warehouse, add a second-person expiry check at each setup, and check other products with future-dated edits (HX-15-30, MR-05-14). Ask the vendor to explain the behaviour. Keep the camera check, because it does verify print against the job. A wider 12-month reconciliation isn't justified now.
